Fresh review of the current claim and complete association set: one ordinary implementation in src/inspector.rs and one TODO test, sage_meta::todo::crates_sage_inspector_inspection_semantic_phase_boundary. No N/A evidence exists. Requirements reviewed independently are semantic completion before serialization/browser rendering, containment of tracked reflection reads in the recorded analysis/reflection boundary, explicit view assembly, and no database access in subsequent JSON/DOM work.

The current product method clears recording before directory/path resolution, runs identity_product inside host.with_context, and only then freezes and retains the generated page and records an Analysis run. Local concrete-ir, signature, typed-ir and diagnostics call reflected_product; external signatures and items call reflected_external_product. Both helpers open the reflection InspectionPhase around reflect_with_references, close it on scope exit, and call assemble_reflected_page afterward. The latter explicitly opens view-assembly and constructs the page from owned values; its database use is the phase log, not tracked semantic reads. Identity and source rendering are constructed explicitly inside the surrounding analysis operation. The resolver is stack-local to reflect_with_references and is used synchronously by value.reflect before finish and continuation extraction. Resolver handling for names, source files, token trees, derive expansions, all generic-parameter families and local/external symbol references performs tracked reads within that scope. Cached references are already owned; stale-directory fallback reference resolution still occurs inside reflection. Continuations are returned as cloned retained trees, not a lazy semantic computation.

Captured current reflection/protocol types show that ValueNode, SymbolReference, ProductPage, RenderNode and ContinuationValue contain owned strings, vectors and scalar/tree data rather than a database or resolver. finish receives an owned tree and continuations clones owned values. The current server product endpoint awaits the product response, then ApiResponse and pretty_json serialize that response with no database parameter. Thus source inspection supports the backend semantic-to-owned-data boundary and establishes why serialization cannot invoke the product resolver. Browser interaction verification is explicitly deferred by the sole associated test, not claimed as exercised here.

The complete TODO function has an empty body apart from its prerequisite comment; it asserts nothing. Its documented outstanding work is to associate and review real-product phase tests, component tests over already-owned trees, and a source-driven browser demand trace covering filtering, resizing, growth, collapse and expansion without semantic requests. This is a justified existing verification deferral: independent phase/no-query assertions and browser-demand observations are required before replacing it with ordinary coverage. No passing placeholder is evidence of those scenarios, and a future late tracked read or semantic request from local UI interaction would not be detected by this function. Acceptance preserves that incomplete test status and does not claim complete end-to-end behavioral verification.

Executed review start with the current coordinator instructions, captured dependency fragments through review read, and inspected current source and the complete associated test. No behavioral tests were run by this reviewer; root owns central test execution. No production/test/association edits or suspected reproduced behavioral failures arose. The source boundary is supported and the existing explicit test deferral is retained without requested edits.
